newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open flat, absorbing economic data.
newsitem.headline: German shares open flat, absorbing economic data.

text.p: German shares opened mostly flat on Thursday after data showing German August money supply growth came in above forecasts and a new business climate index showed confidence improving slightly.
The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares traded 2.84 points lower at 2,622.86, little changed from levels reached in electronic trade before the data was published.

"People are sitting on their hands a bit," said one dealer, noting that the market was now in need of a new impetus to go higher after recent rallies based on the easing of fears of a U.S. interest rate hike.

Although German August M3 measure of money supply grew 8.7 percent compared to forecasts of around eight percent -- in principle countering arguments for another German rate cut -- economists said the growth was largely the result of an increase in short-term credit and thus not too worrying.
"At the end of the day, the bulls will be happier than the bears," one said.
Money supply data was followed by publication of August's business climate index by the respected Ifo Institute which showed a widely-expected but marginal increase in business confidence.
Dealers said they now expected the DAX to remain in a fairly narrow range around the 2,620 point level for the rest of the day.
Among individual stocks, engineering group Daimler-Benz AG was down 80 pfennigs at 82.90 marks, after a steady performance on Wednesday.

Dealers said, however, that sales forecasts and data released by its Mercedes-Benz unit were in line with expectations and not affecting Daimler stock. Mercedes repeated a forecast for 1996 sales of 75 billion marks.
